notes: All 200 ranked candidates have score=0.0, ranking_score=null, plddt=null, ptm=null, iptm=null — the rank_designs step performed a flat/nominal sort with no structural or functional discriminators. The top-20 are reported as required but are not differentiable by score within this run.
GO:0097027 (dehydratase) scan exhausted at 122 accessions before reaching the fill target; only 111 reviewed sequences kept after 2 reviewed_filter drops and 9 unresolved_identifier drops.
GO:0097028 (epimerase) had 62 unresolved_identifier drops and 2 duplicate_sequence drops, yielding 42 reviewed sequences — the epimerase set is considerably smaller than the dehydratase set.

Literature search returned 5 highly relevant records including the foundational Marbaix et al. 2011 JBC paper identifying the ADP-dependent dehydratase and the 2026 Patraskaki zebrafish model paper, confirming the biological target is well-characterized.
One dehydratase sequence (A0A1U8) contains a noncanonical 'X' residue; flagged as unusual_characters liability in seq_analysis_dehydratase output.

Candidate IDs in the ranking output (100, 101, ...) are integer offsets and do not directly expose UniProt accessions; downstream consumers should join against the go_sequences FASTA/metadata artifacts to recover accession-level identity.

plan.goal: Find and analyze representative sequences for NAD(P)HX repair proteins with ADP-dependent NAD(P)H-hydrate dehydratase and NADPHX epimerase activity, then rank representative sequence candidates using available VPA tools
assumptions: GO:0097027 is assigned to ADP-dependent NAD(P)H-hydrate dehydratase activity; if this GO ID is incorrect go_sequences will return zero results and the workflow should be rerun with the confirmed ID from QuickGO before sequence analysis proceeds
GO:0097028 is assigned to NAD(P)HX epimerase activity; same caveat applies
reviewed=true and exclude_iea=true restrict retrieval to manually-curated UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot entries with experimental evidence codes, yielding smaller but higher-confidence sequence sets
Both enzymatic activities belong to the same NAD(P)HX repair pathway so co-ranking across both GO terms is scientifically meaningful for surfacing representative proteins

sequence_analysis operates on the full FASTA produced by each go_sequences node; representative_sequences and top_annotations outputs are forwarded to rank_designs as candidates and analyses respectively

rank_designs aggregates compositional metrics, charge profiles, motif coverage, and biochemical annotations from sequence_analysis as implicit ranking signals; no structure predictions or docking scores are available for this sequence-only task
Literature search runs first to confirm biological context and GO term usage; its outputs inform interpretation but are not programmatically consumed by downstream nodes
